newsitem.title: LATVIA: EU encouraged by Latvian reforms.
newsitem.headline: EU encouraged by Latvian reforms.

text.p: Commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Friday he was encouraged by the pace of reform in the small Baltic state of Latvia as it aims like many of its eastern European counterparts for EU entry.

Latvia is still passing through a tough economic transition period six years after quitting the former Soviet Union and sees EU and NATO entry as vital to cement links with the West and ensure it stays outside the sway of its huge Russian neighbour.
"The reforms already undertaken are encouraging and we expect that they will be consolidated in the short term," van den Broek said in a statement.
He told a news conference he had been impressed by the pace of Latvia's recovery from a serious bank crisis in mid-1995.
"One of the heavy tasks of course is all the legislation to be made compatible with EU legislation," he said.
He also singled out the problem of the large Russian minority in Latvia's 2.6-million population.
Some 600,000 Russian speakers live in Latvia, mostly ethnic Russians, and most of them do not have citizenship.
After independence, Latvia introduced laws which mean most Russians, many of whom were Soviet-era immigrants, have to undergo formal naturalisation to become citizens.
Many have chosen not to naturalise or have to wait until a certain year before they can apply, with the oldest forced to wait longest.
Van den Broek said Latvia needed to make sure that people were not being discriminated against due to the legislation.
